title: Buffett at the 2024 Berkshire meeting: stocks as businesses, patient cash, and one-year insurance risk
summary: Buffett fields shareholder questions on Apple, cash, succession, insurance, utilities and AI. He stresses owning stocks as businesses, swinging only at pitches he likes, compounding retained earnings, pricing insurance risk one year at a time, and being kind and lucky.

principles.text: Treat every stock as a business, not a ticker to trade or time.
principles.quote: when we look at Coca-Cola and American Express and apple we look at them as businesses

principles.text: Hold cash and wait; only act on opportunities you truly like, however big the pile gets.
principles.quote: we only swing at pitches we like

principles.text: Retained earnings plus a long runway compound into enormous wealth without any miracles.
principles.quote: the math of compounding and a long long Runway uh have done wonders

principles.text: Insurance means pricing uncertainty; limit commitments to a year so you can reprice or exit.
principles.quote: if there was no risk there'd be no insurance business and and we're in the business of evaluating it and we do it one year at a time

principles.text: Even for essential, low-return utilities, never invest where you can lose it all.
principles.quote: whether you earn X or go broke is not an equation that works

principles.text: Success is partly luck, so be kind and spread good fortune to others.
principles.quote: if you're lucky in life make sure bunch of other people are lucky
